owe: be obliged to pay or repay
be indebted to, in an abstract or intellectual sense
This new theory owes much to Einstein's Relativity Theory
owl: nocturnal bird of prey with hawk-like beak and claws and large head with front-facing eyes
owlclaws: stout perennial herb of western United States having flower heads with drooping orange-yellow rays; causes spewing sickness in sheep
owlet moth: usually dull-colored medium-sized nocturnal moth; the usually smooth-bodied larvae are destructive agricultural pests
owlish: resembling an owl; solemn and wise in appearance
owlishly: the gentle-looking barrister peered owlishly around him
owlt: the elapsed time it takes for light (or radio signals) to travel between the Earth and a celestial object
own: belonging to or on behalf of a specified person (especially yourself); preceded by a possessive
He owns three houses in Florida
own goal: (soccer) a goal that results when a player inadvertently knocks the ball into the goal they are defending
the own goal cost them the game
own up: admit or acknowledge a wrongdoing or error
the writer of the anonymous letter owned up after they identified his handwriting
owned: having an owner; often used in combination
owner: (law) someone who owns (is legal possessor of) a business
he is the owner of a chain of restaurants
they are searching for the owner of the car
owner's equity: the owner's investment in the business which consists of the net assets of an entity.
The types of accounts and their description that comprise the owner's equity depend on the nature of the entity and may include: common stock, capital surplus, retained earnings, and reserve.
owner-driver: a motorist who owns the car that he/she drives
owner-occupied: one owner-occupied and three rental apartments
owner-occupier: an occupant who owns the home that he/she lives in
ownership: the relation of an owner to the thing possessed; possession with the right to transfer possession to others
the act of having and controlling property
the state or fact of being an owner
